diagnostic_evidence.quote: The penultimate inequality follows from the approximation property of the local $L^2$ projection $\widehat{P}$ on $\widehat{V}_{h,k}$ \cite{RIVIeRE2008}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the face L2 norm of the jump by h^{-1/2} times the broken H^{k+1} norm and then claims the local L2 projection satisfies ||v-\widehat{P}v||_{H^{k+1}} \lesssim h^{k+1}||v||_{H^{k+1}}. The latter is false: the L2 projection is only bounded in H^{k+1}, not h^{k+1}-accurate there, so the displayed chain does not yield the claimed h^{k+1/2} trace rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the trace step with the standard broken trace inequality ||v||_{L2(\partial K)}^2 \lesssim h^{-1}||v||_{L2(K)}^2 + h||v||_{H^1(K)}^2 and use ||v-\widehat{P}v||_{L2} \lesssim h^{k+1}||v||_{H^{k+1}} together with ||v-\widehat{P}v||_{H^1} \lesssim h^k||v||_{H^{k+1}}.
issues.overall_effect: The approximation estimate in Lemma 3.1 is not established as written; its conclusion is true, but the proof contains an invalid inference that must be repaired before the estimate can be used.
issues.title: Lemma 3.1 trace proof uses false H^{k+1} approximation of the L2 projection
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local, standard trace/projection argument; the rate, method, and scope are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate ||u-u\circ\Phi_h^{-1}||_{L2} \le \|id-\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L\infty}\|u\|_{L2} is false; composition differences are controlled by the W^{1,\infty} or H^2 norm, not the L2 norm. Moreover, the final DG estimate discards the h^{2k+1}||\tilde I||_{H^1}^2 term arising from the trace inequality, so the stated bound is not supported and is false for extensions with large H^1 or W^{1,\infty} relative to L2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the composition bounds to \|\tilde I-\tilde I\circ\Phi_h^{-1}\|_{L2} \lesssim h^{k+1}\|\tilde I\|_{W^{1,\infty}} (or H^2) and retain the H1 trace contribution, yielding \|\tilde I-I^\dag\|_{DG} \lesssim h^{k+1/2}(\|\tilde I\|_{H^1}+\|\tilde I\|_{W^{1,\infty}})+h^{k+3/2}\|\tilde I\|_{H^2}, which is absorbable into Theorem 3.1.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.3's stated estimate is false/unsupported, and the T1 boundary consistency estimate in Theorem 3.1, which quotes Lemma 3.3, loses its justification.
issues.title: Lemma 3.3 L2 composition bound is invalid and the H1 trace contribution is dropped
issues.why_classification: The lemma statement must be changed to different norms, but the main theorem survives with an equivalent norm; the repair is contained and causes no loss of the advertised rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts Vol(D_c) \lesssim h^{k+1} 'according to (3.8)', but (3.8) is the Lemma 3.3 error estimate and gives no volume information. The set D_c is a boundary layer of thickness O(h) around the codimension-two characteristic set \Gamma^0_h, so Vol(D_c) \lesssim h^2 independently of k; the claimed h^{k+1} is false for k \ge 2. With the correct volume the displayed T3 estimate only gives O(h^k), so the h^{k+1/2} rate is not established by this argument.

failure_location.quote: For the term $T_3$, let $D_c$ denote the set of boundary elements intersected by the characteristic boundary $\Gamma^0_h$, which means $D_c =\{K\in \mathcal{T}_h:\partial K\cap \Gamma^0\neq \emptyset\}$. By (\ref{eq3.8}), $D_c$ satisfies $Vol(D_c)\\lesssim h^{k+1}$ according to (\ref{eq3.8}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound T3 directly using Area(\Gamma_h^- \Delta \Phi_h(\Gamma^-)) \lesssim h^k and inverse estimates: \|\tilde I\|_{L2(S)} \lesssim h^{k/2}\|\tilde I\|_{W^{1,\infty}} and \|v_h\|_{L2(S)} \lesssim h^{k/2-d/2}\|v_h\|_{DG}, yielding T3 \lesssim h^{2k-d/2} \lesssim h^{k+1/2} for k \ge 2.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary consistency error T3 is not bounded by the claimed rate, so the main theorem's h^{k+1/2} estimate is unproven as written.
issues.title: Theorem 3.1 T3 volume estimate Vol(D_c) \lesssim h^{k+1} is false
issues.why_classification: The false volume claim requires replacing the T3 argument with a different geometric/inverse-estimate bound; the theorem's rate is recoverable, so the loss is limited.
